newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - May 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - May 13.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- GREENWICH SAVERS SET FOR PORTMAN BONUSES

The Portman Building Society yesterday announced it was to take over the tiny Greenwich Building Society, in a deal to be completed by 30 July. About 30,000 Greenwich members will receive bonuses worth up to 2,500 pounds stg per account.
-- POUND RISES AS ERM TALK IS DENIED

The pound made a strong recovery yesterday when Gordon Brown rejected rumours of an intention by the government to take sterling back into the European exchange rate mechanism. After falling to a seven-week low of DM2.7245, the pound closed at DM2.7631.
-- EC TO BLOCK BOEING DEAL

The European Commission is to block Boeing's proposed merger with McDonnell Douglas unless it scraps its exclusive supplier contracts with Delta and American Airlines, European competition commissioner Karel van Miert warned yesterday. Mr van Miert spoke after strong protests over the deal from Airbus.
THE TIMES
-- UK TO END OPPOSITION TO JOB RULE IN TRADE PACTS

The government is to reverse the principal Conservative world trade policy by backing the adoption of minimum job standards linked to trade agreements. Ministers will support pressure for a "social clause" from the US and other nations, likely to be raised at next month's meeting of the G7 nations.
-- NADIR VOWS TO CLEAR HIS NAME AND SUE THE SFO

Asil Nadir is to tell a television audience tonight that he is to sue the Serious Fraud Office for alleged abuse of legal process. The former Polly Peck head is to state in an interview on The Cook Report that he is prepared to return to the UK to clear his name.
-- WATER FIRMS TOLD TO CUT LEAKS OR FACE ACTION

Water industry regulator Ian Byatt yesterday told water firms to cut leaks or face legal action. Speaking on the BBC's Panorama programme, Mr Byatt accused some companies of cutting corners when dealing with leakage. He spoke just ahead of the industry's reporting season, when some companies are expected to announce record profits.
THE GUARDIAN
-- LVMH VOWS TO WRECK MARRIAGE PLAN

French luxury goods group LVMH yesterday declared its intention to destroy the proposed merger between Guinness and Grand Metropolitan. LVMH chairman and Guinness director Bernard Arnault had voted against the plan, suggesting instead that the drinks interests of Guinness, GrandMet and LMVH be merged and listed as a separate company. LVMH said it would use its 14.2 percent stake in Guinness to try and block the deal.
-- GOVERNOR UPBEAT ON CONTROLLING INFLATION

Bank of England Governor Eddie George yesterday spoke optimistically on inflation after the release of figures showing factory goods prices rising at their slowest rate for almost a decade. Mr George said there was a good chance of the government's 2.5 percent target for inflation being reached this year.
-- RAILTRACK LINES UP 580 MILLION POUND LONDON UPGRADE

Railtrack yesterday announced a 580 million pound stg investment to extend the rail network in a 50-mile radius around London. The company will consult with local authorities from Norfolk to West Sussex over the next six months. The plan includes new stations, longer trains and dramatically increased services to ease commuter congestion.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- SIB WANTS GUARANTEES FOR PENSION VICTIMS

The Securities and Investment Board is close to adopting a new scheme aimed at "guaranteeing" redress to victims of the pensions mis-selling scandal. The move came as a report from the Personal Investment Authority, leaked to The Independent, showed insurers are still failing to compensate those worst affected.
-- CO-OP SETTLES FOR 750,000 POUND PAYMENT

The Co-operative Wholesale Society has accepted a settlement of 750,000 pounds stg in return for dropping its civil action against Andrew Regan, Lancia Trust and others over their failed takeover bid. CWS launched its action over the leaking of confidential documents to Mr Regan.
-- DIGITAL TV BID MAY GO TO COURT

The battle to run digital terrestrial television may go to court after British Digital Broadcasting, the bidder encompassing Carlton, Granada and BSkyB, attacked the rival Digital Television Network. BDB said the inclusion of United News & Media in the DTN bid last week contravened Independent Television Commission rules governing changes to applications after the 31 January deadline.
